messages:
Amy K.: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) reports their client hits `Unexpected end of JSON input` when consuming our streamed JSON mode via SSE. They see the last object cut mid-key.
Jordan L.: Can you paste the root request and a small repro? is this happening on all models or a single endpoint?
Amy K.: Repro from customer (sanitized):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-base-1","mode":"json_stream","json_schema":{...}}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They get server SSE events like `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"result\": {\"items\": [\"foo\", \"bar\"`"}}` and then connection closes. Client JSON parse fails.
Sanjay P.: Request id from customer?
Amy K.: `req_0A12BC34`, timestamps attached. They trace through a Cloudflare worker -> our ALB -> gateway. The socket closes before the final `}`. They said it was intermittent (1-2% of streams), higher under burst.
Marie T.: @Jordan L. could this be related to our SSE flush/chunk-size heuristics? I remember a past bug where we would flush partial chunks on idle keepalive.
Jordan L.: Possibly. Need traces from the gateway and the egress TCP FIN sequence. @deploy-bot can you fetch the service logs for req_0A12BC34 and the gateway flush events?
deploy-bot: Fetching logs for request req_0A12BC34 from eng-runtime (this may take a minute) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
(deploy-bot): logs show normal token emits until 14:22:31.839 then `socket: FIN` from client IP after 120s idle. No explicit error on runtime side. Last emitted bytes end mid-object.
Sanjay P.: That pattern sounds like upstream (customer side or CF) actively closing idle connections. Do they have any intermediate proxies that might have shorter idle timeouts? Cloudflare default is 100s for long-poll; their worker code has manual socket close at 120s.
Amy K.: Customer says it happens even on short completions (10–20s) sometimes. They forwarded an nginx reverse-proxy config that has `proxy_buffering on; proxy_read_timeout 30s;` — suspicious.
Jordan L.: Two parallel threads here: 1) intermittent midstream EOFs caused by intermediary timeouts/buffering; 2) our chunking potentially splitting in the middle of a structural token. Short term workaround: ask customer to use non-streaming mode (`mode: json`) to get a single well-formed JSON until we fix. Also recommend setting `Accept: text/event-stream` with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` preserved end-to-end (disable proxy buffering and increase read_timeout).
Marie T.: Longer-term: we should add a runtime guarantee to emit final flush with closing braces as atomic for structured modes — e.g., buffer until the current JSON object is completed before flushing to the wire (within latency SLO). That would hide proxy chopping but may increase tail latency a bit.
Sanjay P.: Agree. For now, engineering should add conservatively-sized last-chunk coalescing for `json_stream` so we don't send partial structural tokens as separate TCP writes. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket.
Jordan L.: Please capture a minimal failing curl that reproduces the mid-object close within 30s so we can CI-test. Amy, can you ask Acme for tcpdump/pcap of the failing session? even a HAR showing truncated last event helps.
Amy K.: Asked for pcap and nginx logs. Also gave temporary guidance: 1) retry with `mode: json` 2) if streaming is needed, set upstream NGINX: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on;` 3) if possible, upgrade to HTTP/2 which preserves streaming better through CF workers.
Jordan L.: Marking this P2 -> P1 because it's causing broken production behavior for a paying account. @Sanjay P. can you assign eng-runtime ticket and add `repro:` label and request a spike to test chunk coalescing? Include request id.
Sanjay P.: On it. Ticket ENG-RUNTIME-4529 opened. Steps: reproduce -> add unit test that injects artificial socket FIN mid-object -> implement coalescing runbook -> measure tail latency delta. Assigning to @Jordan L.
Jordan L.: I'll take the patch. Quick patch plan: coalesce up to 512 bytes or until JSON object completes, whichever first. Also add server-side `last_event: true` SSE metadata and ensure we send a final `data: [DONE]` event before closing. That should reduce parser-visible partials.
Amy K.: I'll keep AcmeCorp updated. Customer asked if they can get a temporary SLA credit; I'll loop in CS for billing. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
